correctness.rationale: Exact Pauli-projector identity gives D=1-|t|/sqrt(t^2+epsilon^2) and L=epsilon^2/(sqrt(t^2+epsilon^2)+|t|). Dominated convergence at fixed nonzero t produces moment exponents 2q below q=1/2, 2p below p=1. Scaling t=epsilon*u with density continuous positive at 0 produces exponents 1 and p+1 above transitions, and intermediate |t|^-1 integrals give logarithms at thresholds. Same-T coupling yields explicit positive finite C_P(theta), C_lambda(theta), with norm mean squares negligible versus epsilon and epsilon^3. Independent high-precision quadrature reproduces both uniform-density exact identities at epsilon=0.1,0.01. The proof, not finite quadrature, covers arbitrary eligible f.
